text:
support_jane: Hey @acme_ops, quick escalation — your rerank calls are returning 429s while generate/embeddings are normal. You said this started when your nightly enrichment job grew candidate count and parallelism. Can you paste an example response and headers? :wave:

acme_ops: Yep. Sample response is below, and headers we capture from our client: we see x-rw-rate-remaining go to 0 mid-run.

acme_ops: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "rerank quota exceeded for customer",
  "retry_after": 45
}
```

acme_ops: Response headers our client logged: x-rw-rate-limit: 200, x-rw-rate-remaining: 0, x-rw-rate-reset: 1775000800

support_jane: Thanks. Engine team, are rerank calls counted differently? Customer assumed token-based billing.

eng_ops_mike: Confirmed: rerank is counted by candidates/items, not tokens. We enforce per-route item quotas to protect latency-sensitive rerank traffic. For this customer we show a soft limit: rerank_items_per_minute=2500 and concurrency_soft_limit=30. The enrichment run spiked them to ~3100 items/minute and ~45 concurrent rerank requests => 429s. :thinking:

eng_ops_mike: Quick math: they sent 62 candidates * 50 requests in one minute ~= 3100 items. If they split into 31 candidates * 100 requests they'd still hit high concurrency.

support_jane: Got it. acme_ops, looks like candidate count + concurrency both contributed. We can apply short-term mitigations and discuss long-term.

billing_sam: Note: their billing dashboard shows tokens only, so this item-based usage didn't surface. Filing SRE task to map rerank items into compute_units usage so customers can see it on dashboard. Ticket: SRE-517.

priya_sre: I'm on SRE-517. Also checking if the quota rules are too aggressive for common PLG customers. Current default protects multi-tenant pools.

quota-bot: Automated action: applied a one-hour soft bump of +40% to rerank_items for account acme-123. Action ID: QB-9931.

support_jane: I told acme_ops we applied a temporary bump and asked them to re-run the job. I also suggested reducing candidate size to <=50 and adding retry/backoff.

acme_ops: Re-ran. We still see occasional 429s but much fewer. Retry-After headers are honored by our client. Thanks.

acme_ops: Can you share a minimal repro script we can run to validate client behavior and to tune backoff?

eng_ops_mike: Sure — two examples. Curl stress loop (bash):

```
for i in $(seq 1 150); do
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["c","c",...repeat to 62]}' &
  sleep 0.15
done
wait
```

eng_ops_mike: Python example with exponential backoff using requests: 

```python
import requests, time
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank'
headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}
payload = {'query': 'x', 'candidates': ['c']*62}
for i in range(200):
    resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        retry = int(resp.json().get('retry_after', 1))
        time.sleep(retry + (2 ** min(i,5)))
    else:
        # process
        pass
```

support_jane: Also watch the response headers: x-rw-rate-remaining, x-rw-rate-limit, x-rw-rate-reset, and Retry-After. Use them to gate retries/parallelism.

billing_sam: Longer-term we should: (1) document rerank counting in billing and quickstart, (2) surface per-route quotas in Console with an apply-for-increase button, and (3) consider offering a rerank-optimized Dedicated pool for high-candidate workloads.

priya_sre: Agreed. I'm adding an action to instrument a per-account breakdown for rerank items in observability so support can debug quickly. ETA: 4 business days. Ticket: OBS-1044.

eng_ops_mike: One subtlety to add to KB: when customers interleave many small rerank requests concurrently, the scheduler enforces both a per-minute item window and a short burst concurrency window. Hitting either will 429; combined hits amplify the rejection rate.

support_jane: For this customer I documented the temporary bump, repro scripts, recommended client changes (reduce candidates, add backoff, limit concurrency), and asked to open a support request if they want a quota change or Dedicated eval. Marking thread actionable with follow-ups: SRE-517 (usage mapping), OBS-1044 (dashboard), KB-299 (support KB with code samples).

acme_ops: Appreciate the quick help. We'll implement backoff and trim candidate size for nightly jobs. Please ping when SRE-517 lands so we can see usage on our billing view. :thumbsup:

support_jane: Will do. Closing thread for now — reopen if 429s reappear after adjustments.
